newsitem.title: USA: Tosco Ca. refinery fire continues to flare up Wed.
newsitem.headline: Tosco Ca. refinery fire continues to flare up Wed.

text.p: The fire that erupted Tuesday night at Tosco's 156,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery in Martinez, Calif., continued to flare up Wednesday, but no new units were affected, a Tosco spokesman said.
"We have had some flare ups a couple times throughout the day," said spokesman James Simmons, attributing them to hydrocarbon seepages in the system.
He added the company plans to let the smaller blazes burn out on their own.
The fire and explosion killed one person and injured 25 when a 32,000 bpd hydrocracking unit, which produces gasoline, blew up late Tuesday.
Tosco and the California Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) have begun separate investigations into the fire's cause, which remains unknown, Simmons said.
The duration of the hydrocracker's shutdown also was uncertain.
"It'll be a while before we can offer a view on that," Simmons said.
Local health officials said no toxin releases or health problems resulted from the fire.
